title: Applied Active Inference Symposium 2025 part 1
transcriptExcerpt: Greetings, everyone. Welcome to the 5th Applied Active Inference Symposium. It's November 12th, 2025. Some brief introduction slides and then to Carl Friston for a keynote address and discussion. So welcome to the Active Inference Institute. We are a non-profit, volunteer-run organization dedicated to improving the rigor, accessibility, and applicability of the Active Inference Framework. Since 2021, we have hosted an annual Applied Active Inference Symposium with Carl as the first presenter back in 2021, which serves as an end-of-year celebration and convening for our ecosystem. At the link symposium.activeinference.institute, you can look at all the previous programs and proceedings. We're here to highlight applied and translational work in Active Inference across domains and from groups around the world. Meanwhile, we service opportunities and needs of our ecosystem, get feedback, and facilitate connections among participants. That's you. And you can watch it live and re-watch it at the same link. And there may be some adjustment at the fine scale with time zones and pre-recorded and live and scheduling and all fun kinds of things. But big picture, there's going to be three live streams that will consist the bulk of the program. In the participant registration, we asked if people wanted their responses to be public. So you can check out that open source code. A big thank you to our team of co-organizers. It's a lot of fun. Email us if you're interested. Also, thank you to our sponsors. Our first sponsor is Navigating Uncertainty, a book bringing the science of active inference and the free energy principle to life through story, art, and human experience by Anna Pereira with a foreword by Carl Friston. So now, without further ado, to Carl's keynote. And I thought, how to introduce this keynote? And on this slide, I have Carl thinking of the 2012 paper, The History of the Future of the Bayesian Brain, where there's a quote, which was about the neuroimaging community, but I believe it applies to the active inference community today as well. And he wrote, in short, the future of imaging neuroscience is to refine models of the brain to minimize free energy, where the brain refines models of the world to minimize free energy.
